History of Present Illness:
___ with hx of multiple admissions for mast cell crises that 
typically involve itching, pain, and wheezing. Patient comes in 
today with her typical symptoms of itching, L chest and 
stomach/back pain, and feeling anxious. She describes her 
symptoms as consistent with past mast cell flares.  
.  
Pt reports recent presentation to ___ with similar 
sx and says was treated with prednisone taper. Gives 
inconsistent story of response to that treatment but claims 
hasn't felt normal since then and has increased appetite on 
steroids. Reports intermittent HA, constipation, diarrhea, 
nausea, chest tighness, wheezing in last 24hrs. Over past week 
has complained of some night sweats and extremity numbness and 
tingling while on steroids. Pt resports finished steroid taper a 
couple days ago.  
.  
According to last DC summaries - there has been concern for pain 
seeking more recently under the guise of "mast cell flares". 
Pt's outpt allergist as well as a ___ consultant have both 
been of belief that last two presentations were unlikely due to 
mast cell flares due to no anaphylaxis, hypotension, or other 
findings that are often present. Pt had been instructed to 
follow-up with her pain physician (Dr. ___ after her 
second to last admission to craft a ___ ___ plan for her 
mast-cell crisis management but had not done this on readmission 
in ___ at which time she became upset when only given one dose 
of IV benadryl and no narcotics. Prior discharge summary 
mentions that there is some in ___ evidence that opiods 
destabilized mast cells and should not be given in these 
settings.  
.  
In ED, initial VS were sig for Temp 98.8, 153/91, HR 80, RR 18, 
Sats 97% on RA. Pt was upset and was given IV benadryl 50mg x2, 
IV lorazepam 2mg x 2, zofran 4mg x 1, and alb-ipra nebs x 2 for 
wheezing. Labs showed mildly elevated alk phos and LDH but were 
otherwise normal (LDH usually normal 200-240 and Alk Phos 
frequently elevated 118-180). CXR showed no acute process and no 
evidence of hyper-expansion. ED was concerned about inability to 
control sx and pt was admitted to the medicine service. VS on 
transfer were HR 72, BP 111/66, RR 18, Sats 99% ra.

Brief Hospital Course:
*Patient Warning* - Be careful about admitting patient for 
symptoms without objective evidence of pathology.

___ yr/o female with PmHx of mast cell degranulation syndrome 
with multiple admissions for "mast cell crisis," who has 
multiple admissions for this despite no objective evidence. She 
is also noted to have "falls" during most recent admission as 
well as past admissions when she does not get the medications 
she wants or is about to be discharged. There had been Recently 
raised concerns regarding drug seeking behavior disguised as 
mast cell flares.  Pt's Allergists (Primary allergist at ___ Dr. 
___ consultant at ___ determined during last 
admission patient was NOT having a mast cell crisis given lack 
of hypotension or anaphylaxis, for which her safety plan from 
___ is supposed to be used for. Pt has a ___ management 
contract from the office of her PCP ___ lists some 
IV medications to be used for her flares, but not if she isn't 
having a flare.  During this admission she was again with stable 
vital signs (afebrile, normotensive, non-tachycardic, satting 
well on RA), no signs of flushing or urticarial lesions on exam, 
and seemed as if was purposefully creating wheezing heard at 
some points during pulmonary exam. More pointedly, she seemed 
more distressed by the fact that her IV medications were going 
to be limited. Pt was discussed with PCP ___ 
agreeded that he did not give IV narcotics or benzodiazapines 
for this issue given no need for them to be  administered in the 
setting of a mast cell crisis.  In fact,  opioid medications 
have been shown to destabilize mast cells in ___, and unclear 
physiologic explanation for why opioids and benzodiazepines 
would help during actual mast cell crisis.  When pt has been 
told that she would no longer require IV Benadryl, she stated 
that she might as well go home. Pt also had multiple "falls" 
during admission which are not believed to be actual falls as 
some were unwitnessed and one "fall" was observed by other 
people down the hall who said the patient gingerly lowered 
herself to the ground and then lay there until the medical team 
arrived and when they arrived claimed she had fallen and hit her 
head. There was never any evidence of fall-induced trauma and 
patient could never give a plausible account of her symptoms and 
the things that would happen when she would fall. Intermittently 
during admission pt would be emotionally labile and cry and 
become frantice when medical team in the room, writhing on the 
bed due to the "pain" she was in. However, when no one was in 
the room pt would be observed laying in bed quietly or talking 
on the phone, seemingly not in any pain. In all likelyhood, it 
would be reasonable to NOT admit her in the future for this 
complaint unless there is objective evidence in the emergency 
department of hypotension or anaphylaxis or hives.

.  
# "Mast Cell Degranulation Syndrome":  
On exam and on labs, there was no evidence of acute mast-cell 
degranulation or other pathologic process despite pt reports of 
itching, abd pain, nausea, and wheezing. Pt had already given IV 
benadryl/benzos in the ED. Pt continued to strongly say that 
only IV benadryl and other IV medications will help. She 
continued to exhibit behavior that is concerning for 
drug/attention seeking as had been noted in past admissions. She 
was given only IV anti-emetics and all other medications were PO 
for her Mast Cell Syndrome (Benadryl, cromolyn spray, 
ranitidine, gabapentin, albuterol/ipratropium nebs). Despite her 
nausea she exhibited no objective vomiting and was able to keep 
pills down. Since there was no evidence of pathology and since 
there were the below mentioned concerns, she was discharged the 
next day on only her home medications.
.  
# Rheumatoid Arthritis:  
Pt on regimen of Etanercept ___ and MTX Qtues along with 5mg 
TID of methadone for pain control. Pt says she is prescribed 2mg 
PO dilaudid Q6hrs PRN pain at home for pain control as well as 
gabapentin, duloxetine. When medication list was checked with 
her PCP, he said patient was not receiving the dilaudid from his 
office and he does not think she takes it as an outpatient. Pt 
was continued on her home medications except for dilaudid since 
it seems likely that patient dose not take this medication
.  
# ADHD/depression/anxiety:  
Pt currently very anxious. She is seen closely by outpatient 
psychiatrist and would prefer to continue following up with him. 
On aripiprazole, duloxetine, and ativan but no longer taking 
modafinil. She was continued on aripiprazole, duloxetine, and 
ativan at home doses during the admission.
.  
# Orthostatic hypotension:  
Has history of this but none noted this admission. Pt on home 
midodrine at 5mg PO TID and this medication continued.
.  
# GERD/gastritis/esophagitis:  
Has history of these and was complaining of epigastric pain 
during this admission although she attributed it to the mast 
cell issue. She was continued on Omperazole and ranitidine as an 
outpatient at high doses.

Discharge Instructions:
Ms ___, you were admitted to the hospital with reports of 
pain, itching, and nausea that you were worried was due to a
